title: Rav Acha bar Huna or bar Rav Huna
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He was Rav Sheshet’s student, as in Bava Batra 70a and Sanhedrin 43a, where he asked Rav Sheshet; he reports “Rav Sheshet said,” as in Berakhot 23a and 32a, Eruvin 20b and 68b, Bava Metzia 33a and Sanhedrin 82b. He was likewise Rabbah’s student, as in Shevuot 36b: Rav Acha bar Huna, Rav Shmuel son of Rabbah bar bar Chana and Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehudah were studying Shevuot in Rabbah’s school; Rav Kahana met them and asked them; Rava bar Nitai said to them, etc. In Menachot 84b, “Rav Acha bar Abba (Hyman proposes bar Huna, Dikdukei Soferim) raised an objection to Rabbah.” He was the messenger between Rav Chisda and Rabbah to bring halakhot from one to the other, as in Pesachim 47a and Yevamot 89b.

Likewise he raised a difficulty against Rav Nachman, as in Chullin 76b. In Nedarim 90a: a man vowed not to marry until he had learned halakhot, and he could not, and wished to annul his vow. Rav Acha bar Rav Huna came, misled him and married him to a woman, and afterward brought him before Rav Chisda to annul his vow; and Rava said: “Who is wise enough to do such a thing, if not Rav Acha bar Rav Huna, who is a great man?”

Hyman suggests that apparently he was a judge in his town, as implied in Kiddushin 12b: a man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the market; Rav Acha bar Huna sent before Rav Yosef: “In such a case, what?” He sent him: “Flog him, according to Rav,” etc. He was friendly with all the great men of the generation, with Abaye and Rava, as in Shabbat 124a and Bava Batra 116b, where he sat with Rav Safra, Rav Huna bar Chanina and Abaye. More than all, he discussed matters with Rava: he raised objections to Rava, as in Menachot 16a and 71b and Chullin 32b; posed contradictions to Rava, Shabbat 103a; and asked Rava, Kiddushin 56b. When Ifra Hormiz sent an offering to Rava to sacrifice for her, Rava sent Rav Safra and Rav Acha bar Rav Huna to carry out the matter according to law, as in Zevachim 116b, and Abaye too was there (Hyman therefore dates this before Rava headed the academy). And what we find in Shabbat 66b, that he raised a difficulty against Rav Ashi, Hyman considers a scribal error and proposes, according to Dikdukei Soferim, Rav Acha son of Rava.
He left after him a son, a Torah scholar, named Rava, as in Niddah 31b.

notes.text: The full Berakhot23a returned chain supports Acha reporting Sheshet; supplied Nitai remains against the returned Shevuot37a Itai, not harmonized. Hyman’s Menachot barHuna proposal and Shabbat Acha-son-of-Rava proposal remain scoped alternatives. The messenger direction, vow strategy, sacrifice delegation, chronological aside and Rava son are preserved.

The consulted Berakhot 23a directly nests Acha bar Rav Huna’s transmission under Sheshet. Shevuot 36b ends in the middle of Kahana’s question; the complete 37a continuation names Rava bar Itai, while Hyman prints Nitai. Preserve both. His messenger, vow-strategy and sacrifice-delegation accounts and proposed Menachot/Shabbat names remain occurrence-specific, not general name harmonization.
